title: Getting to Know the System

slides.text:
When you open the app, you arrive at the homepage.
From here, enter the library—this is where your slideshows will live.
The first time you enter the library, you’ll be taken to the Examples page because you don’t have a workspace yet.
Click “Create your workspace” to begin.
Your workspace is your own section of the library, where your slideshows will live. You can create as many workspaces as you need.
When you enter your workspace, you can click New Slideshow to start a project from scratch.
But if this is your first time, the easiest way to learn is to begin with one of the example slideshows.
The Examples workspace is read-only, so the original slideshows cannot be changed.
Choose an example you like and copy it into your own workspace. Now you can experiment with it freely.
Open the copied slideshow and start experimenting.
Try changing an effect or transition, adjust some of its parameters, and press Play to see what happens.
Changing something and immediately seeing the result is one of the easiest ways to become familiar with the system.
Think of each slide as being built from layers.
You can add images, sounds, and other elements on separate layers, then adjust each one independently.
Let’s begin with one of the most useful kinds of layers: a foreground image.
To begin adding a foreground image, click + Add Foreground Layer.
For most foreground images, it is useful to use an image with a transparent background. This allows the layers behind it to remain visible.
You can also use several foreground layers to build a scene from separate elements.
You can apply an effect to a visual layer to change how it appears or behaves.
To add an effect, open the Effects Hub.
This is where you can explore the different visual effects available in the system.
Select an effect that interests you to open its controls.
Each effect has its own parameters, allowing you to change how it behaves.
The easiest way to understand an effect is to experiment with it.
Change a parameter, add the effect to your slide, and press Play to see the result.
Change a parameter, add the effect to your slide,
and press Play to see the result.
Transitions work in a similar way, but they control what happens when one slide ends and the next begins.
You can choose a basic transition directly,
or open the Transitions Hub for more advanced options.
Choose a transition
adjust its parameters,
and press Play to see how it changes the movement from one slide to the next.
The system is open-source, so you are not limited to the effects and transitions that already exist.
If you need something different, you can create your own custom effect or transition and add it to the system.
Because the project is open-source, you can open it in an AI coding environment and extend it yourself.
The system helps you describe what you want to create and generate a prompt.
All you have to do is bring that prompt into an AI coding environment, where your idea can be turned into a new form of expression.
This gives you the freedom to create new effects, transitions, and other tools when the existing ones do not express what you need.
When your slideshow is ready, you can export it together with its player.
The export creates a webpage and its supporting folder, so the slideshow can be viewed outside the application.
In addition to running independently, the exported slideshow also serves as a portable backup.
After experimenting with an example slideshow, begin creating a simple slideshow of your own.
Explore the available options, make changes, and press Play to see how your choices affect the result.
The tools already in the system are only a starting point.
The medium is designed to grow through the people who use it.
Use the tools already available. Combine them, experiment with them, and discover what they can express.
When the existing tools are not enough, create new ways to express what you want to communicate.
As more people create and share these new forms of expression, together we can develop a richer language.
A language for communicating ideas, feelings, and intentions.
One that can express meaning beyond what words alone can carry.

description: Learn the system step by step by exploring examples, editing slides, and seeing how image, sound, timing, effects, and transitions work.
